metadata.title: Crypto VC Firm Dragonfly Promotes Rob Hadick and Tom Schmidt to Managing Partners

content.text:

ights - Dragonfly promoted Rob Hadick and Tom Schmidt to managing partners, joining Haseeb Qureshi and Bo Feng.

Hadick previously worked at GoldenTree Asset Management, Goldman Sachs, PJT Partners and Heritage Partners.
-
Schmidt previously led product at 0x and worked at Facebook, Instagram, Apple and Microsoft.
In a major update, Crypto venture capital firm Dragonfly has promoted Rob Hadick and Tom Schmidt to managing partners, expanding its leadership team to four now.
Haseeb Qureshi, managing partner at Dragonfly, announced the promotions in a post on X on October 28. Hadick and Schmidt will lead the firm alongside Qureshi and co-founder Bo Feng.
"Both Tom and Rob have been central to building the firm into what it is today, from the deals we've led, our leadership in industry, to the founders we've stood behind through every cycle," Qureshi wrote.
He added that the firm's mission remains unchanged: "backing the founders building the future of money and markets."
The leadership change becomes more important as Dragonfly has established itself as a prominent investor among the top cypto VC firms, backing companies like Polymarket, Ethena, Agora, Rain, Monad, among others.
Who are Dragonfly's new managing partners?
Dragonfly's new managing partner Rob Hadick brings experience in traditional finance, private investments and digital assets to his new role.
Before joining Dragonfly as Managing Partner, he was serving Dragonfly in General Partner role for the past 4 years. He has helped lead crypto investments at GoldenTree Asset Management, a multi-strategy investment firm, where he worked on investments in public and private crypto companies.
Earlier in his career, Hadick held roles spanning technology, fintech and investment advisory at Heritage Partners, Goldman Sachs and PJT Partners. His background combines traditional financial markets with experience evaluating businesses across the digital asset ecosystem.
His linkedin describes him as an investor in companies like Polymarket, Rain and he also sits as a board member on startups like Velocity, Agora, Mesh.
Tom Schmidt, meanwhile, brings a product and engineering background alongside his experience in crypto investing. Before joining Dragonfly, Schmidt led product at 0x, an Ethereum-based decentralised exchange protocol, and worked as a product manager at Facebook and Instagram.
He also held engineering roles at Apple and Microsoft. His experience building technology products and working with blockchain infrastructure gives him a different perspective on the companies Dragonfly backs.
